steps.right: None, private cost is the only cost

steps.q: Using marginal analysis, output should keep expanding only while one more unit adds more to society's benefit than it adds to society's cost. At what output does that stop being worth it?
steps.right: Where marginal social benefit equals marginal social cost
steps.wrong: Where total revenue is at its highest

steps.q: Now suppose making this good also pollutes a river, so social cost is higher than the factory's own private cost at every output. If the factory only ever weighs up its own private cost against demand, will it stop at the same output as the one where MSB equals MSC?
steps.right: No, it will produce more than that
steps.wrong: Yes, it will stop at exactly that output
